text: Defective GE Unitized Stackable Washer/Dryer. We purchased a similar GE Unitized washer and dryer in July 2014 that already broke.The repair man told us it needs almost a $1,000.00 in repairs and he wouldn't bother since they have so many problems. It is the third one he has seen the same repairs on just this year, transmission rusted, engine rusted, bearings are bad and more. Do not waste your money. The only help GE offered by Travis in consumer relations was to charge us another $99.00 to come out to diagnose it again. Then charge us to repair it at a possible discount. After paying $1,200.00 just 2 years ago, it obviously a problematic washer/dryer. So PLEASE do not buy GE and make the same mistake we did.

Buyer's Remorse. We bought a LG front-loading washer two and a half years ago after researching a number of different washers and reading good reviews on this particular one. Lately, it has been leaking water and suds under the washer. Attempts to get LG "customer service" to resolve the issue were unsuccessful. I feel this company did not stand behind it's product. I don't plan on buying any other LG product in the future.
Shakes during spin after less than 1 year of use.. After less than 1 year the washer shakes in the spin cycle.

Works all right, but is easily unbalanced and occasionally skips the spin cycle.. We bought this washer and the accompanying dryer about six months ago, after a disastrous set of Maytags started having problems within a week of purchase. It works well enough, but no matter how carefully you load it, it seems to bang its way through the spin cycle - when it actually bothers to get to the spin cycle. About 1 time in 5, it seems to skip the spin altogether. It's easy enough to turn it straight to the spin and hit start when that happens, but still. Others have mentioned issues with the auto-fill not providing enough water to get the clothes clean - I noticed this at first and now always use the manual water level selection and usually the 2nd rinse option. Not very water-saving at that point, but at least the clothes are clean! Also, it does make a slight repetitive squeaking noise when agitating that is apparently just a normal part of operation. Not a big deal for us, and the eventual banging of the unbalanced spin cycle is much louder anyway, hahaha! In retrospect, I miss the Kenmore stack we left behind when we relocated and rented out our old house. Didn't know it would be so difficult these days to find a washer that worked simply and well!

Piece of Junk!!!!. This washing machine does not clean. It takes forever to wash and when your are finished the clothes are not clean. My husband farms and my kids play a lot of sports. I cannot get the clothes clean with this machine. DO NOT BUY A WASTE OF MONEY!!!! I use it everyday and dislike it more and more. Just wash new sheets. Got them out of the washer the top of sheet was completely dry in spots. How can it clean when it doesn't even wet all the clothes. What a waste of money!!!!!!

Not TOO bad but I'm not happy with it. Actually bought this from Sears and had it delivered and installed including metal vent pipe and stainless steel gas hose for about $25 less than advertised here BUT... It just 'cra**ed out after almost 10-mo. and I was relieved to read that the GE warranty was for a year parts and labor but right now I'm into day 4 of waiting 2-4 days for parts to come to the repair person[s] and just called and learned that the last part's supposed to arrive today and that maybe the repair can be made in 3 more days which will be a day after we need to use it. Maybe I should have called Sears but I didn't. The repair agent is in a city quite a way from here and I'm told that they have a couple of people in our city to do their work. So it appears that GE has a loose network of repair agents and repair persons and that we MAY get repaired in a week from first contact. Not TOO bad but I'm not happy with it. And this just a month or so after a buddy's GE washer bit the dust in less than a year. Do I sense a trend?

BUYER BEWARE -. Shame on Samsung for deceptive marketing! As another reviewer has already stated, the info page on Samsung's site is EXTREMELY DECEPTIVE. The website lists in four different places that this machine has wifi capabilities. Nowhere is there an asterisk or notation that YOU NEED TO BUY AN ADDITIONAL PART to make it capable of wifi. We tried calling Samsung multiple times to give them the opportunity to make it right and were given the run around each time. They refuse to acknowledge the deceptive marketing. The machine works great, just know that it DOES NOT HAVE WIFI CAPABILITIES unless you shell out more cash for a difficult-to-find part.

Worst Washing Machine. This is the worst washing machine I’ve ever owned. We’ve had it fixed twice in 2 years and it still doesn’t work properly. The clothes smell after they are washed and very few clothes can be washed per cycle. I would definitely avoid this washing machine.

Stay away from Whirlpool Cabrio... didn't last 3 years. We relied on consumer reports as the primary source for a recommendation on this washer. Just under two years old, it started making a noise, which suddenly went away. Then one day the machine would not spin and drain, and we could not decipher the error code into anything useful. I turned the machine over to find that the drive belt was half-on/half off the pulley on the drive motor. This caused the belt to ride against the belt guard and wear right through it. I removed the belt and determined that the cause of the problem was that the large pulley on the drum was loose. For some reason the nut which holds that pulley on was slightly loose, causing the pulley to wobble. Not sure why they didn't use some loctite on that nut. I put everything back together and tightened the nut. No problems and I checked it a month later, everything was still good. Fast forward to last week, when the machine was not yet 3 years old. Same thing, washer would not spin and drain. Tipped machine over to find that the belt had fallen off, the drum pulley was again loose. But this time the belt had damaged the pulley on the motor. I figured, no problem, just order a new pulley. Well you can buy just the pulley on the drum, but the pulley on the motor is part of the motor, it cannot be ordered by itself. The cheapest I could find the motor online was $250. We decided to cut our loses and buy a new machine. We will NEVER buy another whirlpool appliance (or anyone else's by the same manufacturer, i.e. maytag). Our last kenmore washer lasted 23 years. Oh but it had an agitator and wasn't listed as HE (High Efficiency), so I suppose the environmentalists would get the dry heaves thinking about the impact of that washer on the environment. But it was useful for 23 years. Now this HIgh Efficiency whirlpool is headed for the recycling pile. Sorry, I think this hurts the environment more than an appliance which just works year after year. Yep, they took a design that worked and now we have energy/water efficient washers that don't last very long and are so expensive to repair that the solution is to just buy a new one.
Larger than expected!. Perfect for my needs! I am older and am arranging for 1 floor living. It is compact and operates quietly! Love it!

Propane fuel - buyer beware. If you plan on using this dryer with LP, a conversion kit is required, does not come with the unit, and needs to be installed by a licensed technician - dramatically increasing the installed cost of the unit

There is a law suit against this washer.. Who ever wrote the previous review is 100% correct. I have this washer and I am going through the same problem. This is the washer that was recalled. The solution is either fix it and get one year warranty from that date or give you the depreciation amount for it which is not equal to buying a new one. I told them to fix. This took at least 4 months with 3 different technicians trying to do so. After it was fixed, it is still making noise, and stopping in middle of the cycle. It will start washing your clothes, will take all the time necessary to do so, and when done, you will see lot of flashy lights. Once you open it, your clothes will be soaked with water and not done. I usually repeat this process 3 or 4 times, then I would need to change the load, meaning I have to do the current one by hand, and put a smaller one instead, it finally works. I have a son and need to do lot of laundry. I feel that I spend more time with this washer than with my son. This morning, I received a notice in the mail of a Proposed Class Action Settlement against this Samsung top load Washing Machine. You can have more info at: www.washermdlsettlement.com Too bad, I cannot receive any benefit from it because they want documentation of every penny spent. Samsung, please refund me my money so I can buy a new washer. I am not even asking for all the money that I spent washing our clothes outside for the 6 months while this machine got "fixed" the first time.

Love it..... Was going to answer the one star review. Didn't see a way to post a picture. So did this review instead. Gee... Any washer is a risk of water leakage. Even a large amount. Most of the time, that's all I have ever seen is a large amount. That's why I traded in my old washer for one very similar to this. A WM2101HW. Inserting picture. Bought used from a repair shop. Gee... Mine is in the basement. Has a drain in the floor right in front of it. If it didn't. I'd always worry with any washer. I m happy as can be with mine. It washes better. Efficient as can be. I'm happy as can be. I also set mine up with a water recycling system. I pump the used water out on my lawn. I can fit 8 washes in the two barrels. Makes it easy. I also don't use a dryer. This one helps by spinning the clothes dryer. It is very dry here. Works good for hanging clothes up. So in the end.... I have an extremely efficient wash system that I'm happy as can be with.

None-in-One. The good thing about this machine is that it's two useless appliances, but only takes the space of one. And it's beautiful too! In true Rube Goldberg fashion, the machine goes on for 5-6 hours at a time, with beautiful LED readouts, wonderful spinning & gyrations, while accompanied by the gentle hum of percision engineering -- and amazingly enough, at the end of all this, your clothes are damp, dirty and wrinkled (even with a small load.) It should also be noted that your patience is rewarded with the musty odor imparted into your clothes that apparently only a 5 hour dry cycle can achieve.
Five Stars. Years after purchase still working great! Thannks

DO NOT BUY. We purchased this machine in December 2011 and now (May 2015) is has developed a vibration that moves it around the room. I leveled several times and did all the regular troubleshooting. Then thought it might be the internal shock absorbers. Finally found out that this machine develops a problem with its flange adapter (it breaks) after about 4 years. Google it. There are lots of reported cases. We didn't even make it to fours years. What a HUGE waste of money. It worked nicely for a few years but that is far too little time when you're spending hundreds of dollars on a major appliance.

Great Dryer. Had to replace a 19 year old Amana gas dryer. Was not having any issues over the years, but the dryer started making bad sounds and stop running. Did a lot of shopping, looking and reading to see if there were any obvious choices that should be made due to advantages. Not seeing anything that stood out, we looked at the features we had to have. Gas, sensor drying, front side lint filter and interior dryer light. The dryer installed easily, was exceptionally quiet and dried the clothes very quickly compared to the dryer it replaced. Seems solid and has some nice features, no buzzer, more like a cell phone jingle at the end of the cycle. Lots of choices for temperatures and dryness levels.

Love this dryer!. This dryer is awesome! I got a great deal on it when I bought it along with the matching washer. This dryer works awesome and gets my clothes dry quickly. It runs quietly and plays a song at the end of the dry cycle instead of the usual annoying buzz! One thing to know about this dryer is that I usually have to set the automatic dry to "more dry" instead of "normal." The normal setting has almost always ended up with clothes that are still a little damp. It is a minor annoyance and something I don't even think about now. This dryer looks confusing at first with so many buttons and the dial as well as a display, but you will quickly find that the controls are easy to figure out and make lots of sense! You will be efficiently drying your clothes in no time!
Four Stars. We are really happy with this unit thus far, we have been using regularly now for 6 months.

Samsung front load washer and dryer have been the worst appliance investment I have made in 30 years. Rating should really be a zero. Samsung front load washer and dryer have been the worst appliance investment I have made in 30 years. Repairs at least twice a year and after 4 years I have nearly paid for a new machine in repair bills. Repair company also told me they are the worst machines on the market but keep them in business with constant repeat calls for repairs on new machines. Average life span (according to the repair companies is 4 years). Mine will be headed to the dump after only 3 years and over $800 invested in repairs. I hope I can prevent someone from making the same mistake I made. I will NEVER purchase another Samsung product again.

Love My washer!. We bought this washer when it first came out. I was a little nervous about spending so much, but I am so pleased with it! We have never had a problem and it does a great job cleaning. I can wash my quilts a bunch of jeans, and all our winter coats!I don't need to take them to the laundromat or cleaners! My only problem is that I didn't buy the dryer and now I don't know where I can get it!

Outstanding machine.. This is the best wash machine I have ever owned. I hope they never stop making it. It has an agitator, the lid does not lock, so you can rinse out the soap cup before you put it back on the detergent container. It will allow you to adjust the settings how you want them set. Everything about this machine is great. Most important, it cleans my clothes. Stay away from those machines that don't have an agitator.
It’s great. Wish it had a regular lint catcher thingy but other than that this thing is awesome

Bad Machine!. We bought ours in 2008 and have come here to warn people not to purchase. within 2 years the sensor that controls the machine draining went out it is such a common part to break that it was back ordered and we had to wait for over a month to get the washer fixed. Now it's making the loud noise in spin cycle. I just had the "whirlpool" repair man come look at it. I paid him 140.00 just to tell me to buy a new washer. I was quoted 1650.00 just to get it fixed. No thank you I could buy 2+ washers for that price. I will never buy whirlpool again. a one year warranty on this machine is a joke!
Disappointing. Bought this washer to be energy efficient. Have not noticed any savings and it does a poor job of cleaning. Its matching dryer has been great, but this was a waste of money.

Took me awhile, but it grew on me. My experience with this washer was rough going for the first month or so. Many of those first loads had a horrible odor...the clothes and the tub. I like the function of the settings. I like that it's programmed to a 'normal' setting that we typically use. One of my children thinks every load should be on quick wash (which I don't like). On our old machine, I wouldn't notice that he had turned the knob until I had done a load or two. On this machine, he can put it on quick cycle and it will automatically return to the 'normal' setting that I like for the next load. After I run whites set on bright white with hot water, the next load automatically goes back to the preset program. I like that it's top load. That's one less bending stress that my back doesn't need. I've never liked the front load. I like the see-through top. It's interesting to me to see just what's going on in there. I guess it's the child in me. Even though the barrel is deep, I have no problem reaching in to unload. I'm 5'6", but two of my children are several inches shorter. They have no problem removing clothes as well. The child in me also likes the tune it plays when a load is finished. It does take longer to run through the cycles, but that's okay with m because the clothes come out much dryer. The spin cycle really gets the water out, which takes less time to dry. Initially I gave this a 3 star rating. That was completely based on the 'stink'. The only problem is that I simply could not believe how bad they smelled at first. I've done a lot of research on this and have found that this is often a problem with high efficiency machines because they don't use as much water. My previous high efficiency washer never left clothes smelling at all...never ever. To manage that, I sometimes add vinegar to the bleach compartment. I know sounds crazy right? Vinegar has a million uses. This is annoying to be sure. Were it not for that, it would be a 5 star for sure. I gave it a 4 star, however, because of its rocky start. I should finally add that now, after a couple of months, I haven't had any loads that were unbalance or smell at all. I've also washed tennis shoes a couple of times and it was not a problem at all. So all in all, its' turned out to a great washer.

Do no buy it, buy any brand low cost front loader instead. This was one of my biggest mistakes in a long time. After the first washes, I started to see residual suds in the garments and then shredded shirts and ripped towels. Since I am one of those anal engineers I decided to see what was going on by defeating the lid with a mild magnet to see what was going on which shocked me. The first wash cycle is fine and smooth but when the machine cycles into the final rinse and spin cycle the fill level is only 7-8 of cold water and the agitator beats the crap out of any long garment by violently rotating back and forth (the longer the garment, the worst the damage) by pulling and tearing the clothes against each other, bed sheets faired the worst. Frustrated I called GE customer support to see if I could control the rinse cycle water level but he told me that GE engineers were forced to do that because of Government efficiency regulations and that the machine is electronically programed to do just that and cannot be changed. I am now stuck with a GE machine that will poorly rinse my clothes so I have to run them thru once more thru a normal cycle which wastes twice more water despite our wonderful Government regulations while tearing up my China made clothes which I must buy more often so who is the winner at the end? Certainly not the US. I not only blame myself for not doing my research before buying but also the dumb Government and the lazy GE engineers that just took a regular non HE washer and just programmed with less water on the rinse/spin cycle without thinking about the consequences to customers like me which are beginning to hate badly designed machines with poor quality, no wonder the US is loosing to foreign made machines. How sad.
One Star. A real lemon. Owned 18 months and have already had to have it serviced 3 times.
Great. Very good washer

It worked fine for the first year. We bought this extra-large capacity washer because we do a lot of wash. It worked fine for the first year, but soon after the warranty ran out, it took a dive. Now every load of wash stops multiple times with an out-of-balance error. LG says it is our fault - that we shouldn't be putting towels in with socks, and that we need to put more than two pounds of items in to make it work. We've tried everything - leveling the washer, adding ant-vibration pads, and trying all different size loads, including the recommended tub clean or empty load. The error stops the load every time. The technician who is LG-certified says he can't do anything about it, and says that LG's are very sensitive - they go out-of-balance very easily. That doesn't help me. I can't get any help from LG. I've spent hours on the phone with them. I'm ready to give up and buy a new non-LG washer. I've put over a thousand dollars into this machine, and it takes about ten hours to wash a load of wash. So disappointing.

Good Luck! This is comparable to needing to change .... Eventually, the drain filter will need cleaned. Good Luck! This is comparable to needing to change an oil filter on a car, it will need to be done only good luck getting to it! The washer will stop working and flash an Error code and the Users Manual is next to worthless in leading to the cause and silent on how to resolve. There is no support on the Bosch site and the dearth of info and the perplexing engineering makes this prime fodder for an unhappy time. I've invested 3 hours so far and don't even have the front panel off. If anyone knows how to get the friggin front panel off (the 3 torque screws are out but it wont budge), please post. Otherwise, the washer has worked well which is why it gets 2 stars.

Huge disappointment. We bought this machine about a year ago. Doesn't rinse clothes. Constantly throws error codes. We bought it to replace the cheapo Goldstar top loader we had before. That thing was ten times the machine this one is at 1/3 the cost. Now its back to the 60 year old wringer washer we use every time another new washer craps out. Thanks for the lesson in caveat emptor whirlpool.

Complete garbage!!. Prepare yourself for terrible customer service. You will also be replacing all 4 suspension rods sooner rather than later (read the reviews, this is a universal issue with this machine). Garbage washer made with cheap parts. Save your money and look at a more reputable manufacturer.

Good High Efficiency Washer but Much Louder than Expected. This machine gets my clothes clean, uses less water, detergent, and electricity than my last machine and has a huge basket. The basket does not fill all the way but I have ran some pretty big loads and have not noticed any spotting or problems with my clothes. The power rinse option seems to compensate for not filling the basket all the way. My preferred setting is the manual fill Super Load, with cold water for colors and warm for whites and I always use the PowerRinse option. Only drawbacks I've noticed is that the machine is much louder than I expected it to be (especially when the agitator is running) and that it took forever to ship from the dealer I ordered it from. These are the reasons I only give it a four star. Owned it for a little over a month now though and no major complaints thus far. I called GE on the noise and they said this should decrease with time and is completely normal when breaking in a new wash machine. Time will tell.

Very disappointed. This is my fourth Whirlpool washer. Very disappointed. This is my fourth Whirlpool washer. They have always impressed me with their dependability. But this machine is only 2 years old and it has developed the dreaded F5E3 Error....may be the lid lock...$250... or might be the system Board...$$$$$$$$$!

Horrible. this is the worst machine I have ever had after 40 years of using washing machines. I have had it for 2 months and it is the loudest machine. My sheets come out twisted and thumps with every load even though it has been balanced. I am having the service man come this week. Thinking about selling and getting a Speed Queen.

and it smells better already. We going back to a top loader .... Just had this thing removed from my house, and it smells better already. We going back to a top loader with as few features as possible. This Electrolux washer was good for one month, then, that front loader smell started creeping in. By the fourth month, we were running the exhaust fan constantly trying to air out the room, keeping the door open, doing everything from A to Z to try and control the smell. We replaced the boot which we found had a tiny tear in it, thinking that it might be part of the problem. The smell just got worse. I can't imagine how much electricity we wasted trying to ventilate that room, dumping 200 cubic feet per minute of air conditioned air this summer. Boot #2 ripped to pieces (literally) when a washable pillow got wedged in it, and the washer started to leak. It's gone now at less than one year. Although, we got good warranty service... I just wanted to be done with this type of washer. We have the matching dryer, which is working fine for us.
Total Disappointment.. Total disappointment, stopped working just after one year, have had two repairs and am now wishing we had just replaced it.

Expensive launtry room ornament.. Continues to leak through the vent and LG continues to tell me to much soap or the wrong soap. I am not an idiot. Read the other reviews and complaints about this exact problem. Currently using trace amount of soap and tried changing brands. Repeat maintenance and cleaning procedures in one half the recommended intervals. This model needs a class action.

Nope...never again. This machine is leaking water like a sieve with every single load. I have been waiting for 3 weeks for someone to identify the issue and actually fix it. It is coming from the bottom. No, I do not use a ton of soap (I have been told use only HE...no problem, then ...don't fill more than the imprinted marking on the machine itself...no problem...now being told only a TSP of liquid....are you kidding me?....are you telling me this hi-tech machine will freak out if I use more than a TSP of liquid soap for an entire load of clothes?) No, it is not user error. For such an expensive machine it should actually wash the clothes withOUT leaking. As an added headache. The service technicians had the parts delivered to my home without any notice (parts, mind you, that never corrected the leaking complaint). I am talking about boxes so large the UPS guy had to make a special trip and then use a dolly to get it in my garage a 4.5ft giant unwieldy cube. THEN to add insult to injury, the techs would not remove the boxes, and old parts. Who does that? The trash service won't pick up these pieces/parts curbside, and it won't fit in my car to go to a dump. I'm not trying to be nitpick-y here but come on! So here I sit, with boxes, parts, crazy amounts of packing material, a flooded laundry room floor and mounds of laundry piling up. Hey LG, how bout a little help getting this issue squared away?

Black Mold Growth. I’ve used this washer for couple of years and am having a serious black mold growth inside the gasket within the folds. Recently my cloths started to smell odd after a fresh wash and eventually my dryer heater stopped working. After calling a local appliance repair company to repair the dryer. They pointed out the mold issue on the washer. I didn’t believe I had mold since it wasn’t visible and I use bleach to wash white regularly however he flipped the gasket between the door and washer tub which exposed a large amount of black mold growth. There is also black mold growth in the detergent dispenser area. The cost to remove the mold and replace the gasket where the mold growth originated is about the cost of a new top loader. I contacted LG and they said I needed to replace my gasket if the mold is not removable using bleach and water. They are aware of the issue but pointed out the warranty card where the gasket is not covered under warranty. I asked about the new design that resists mold growth from online forums write ups I read and they gave me the part number to purchase. I’ve had many washers in my life and never had to worry about adding mold after a fresh wash. I have a toddler that’s been wearing cloths washed in black mold mixture thanks to this washer.

JUNK!!!!’. JUNK!!! After 2.5 years the motor went bad- Not covered under warranty. Even though front label says “10 year warranty on motor”. Prices to get fixed 400.00 . I’ve had other machines that have last 10-20 years! This is a piece of JUNK!!!!

Walks out the laundry room door.... ...down the hall and talks with the LG frig who is never shy about answering. When our previous washer may have died (we hated it and swore at the first hint of trouble it was out the door) we were thrilled to get this new one. The thrill lasted about 3 washes and we cried to have our old one back. There is no such thing as a balanced load of anything larger than socks - OK - t-shirts also, if they're the same size, weight, and style. And do not put a pair of socks in with sheets - you will be sorry. Every load shudders, and most have walked the machine substantially out of position. The wash times (thanks to HE) are extravagant - many over 90 minutes, during which I have glued myself to it waiting to see if it will walk. Do not run a load and think you can run errands while it's washing. Several times I have given up trying for any spin and just thrown it all in the dryer. IF you are successful with a wash, rinse and spin, and maybe even the extra rinse and spin, check to make sure you actually put your laundry in it. Yes, it was professionally installed. Yes, it is level in every direction, we check it after each use, because it violently shudders even if it doesn't walk. Yes, it is on risers. Yes, our floor is stable and level. Our only solutions are work-arounds. Pretty sad situation for the money spent.

Excellent quality washer with a few minor drawbacks. Purchased locally from BBuy, used for 6 months prior to giving a review. Pros: 1. Very water efficient. I was switching from the 5-yr old top-loader Whirlpool. This Samsung weights each load to determine the optimal amount of water. 2. Washes great even with cold water! (save on energy) 3. Easy to use, very intuitive. Drawbacks: 1. I placed the washer in the pan (to avoid flooding the floor in case of machine breakdown - paid $20 some dollars at HomeDepot). The pan limits how wide the drain compartment door opens and as a result makes draining and filter cleaning somewhat inconvenient. (Cleaning is required every couple of months. I cleaned once, but there was so little debris/dirt in the filter. Given this and the inconvenience of cleaning, I will clean it again in 6 months. Clean the pockets to minimize the dirt in the filter. 2. Some water is being accumulated in the rubber sealant ring around the cover door - I am talking good couple of ounces. As I can imagine, if it's left unwiped, the moisture can grow into mildew. No big deal to wipe it off after each use, but I thought it was worth warning. 3. I searched left and right for the stacking kit for this washer and compatible dryer, but the only place that is selling them is samsung autorized part distributor - samsungparts.com. I went to Sears but they refused to sell me the kit cause they didn't sell me the washer/dryer. BestBuy did not have any in stock anywhere in the MidAtlantic region. Had to call samsung directly and was directed to the above mentioned website. *************** I uploaded a bunch of pictures with notes - make sure you check them out **************
Love it! Easy to use. Only used as washer - works great as a washer. Can dry laundry that is not bulky like jeans and towels.

Whirlpool Duet Washer. In January of 2009 we purchased a Whirlpool Duet washer and dryer set from East Coast Appliance in Newport News, Virginia. In October 2010 the washer started to make a significant noise when the drum was spinning. We had a service technician check the washer and he advised us the drum and rear tub shell needed to be replaced. I called your customer service personnel and was advised that the only remedy they could provide was a 50% discount on parts. On Dec 1st I talked to Tasha at Whirlpool and ordered the two parts. I asked for email confirmation on the order and Tasha stated she would do that. I also left several phone numbers as contacts. All of the phones have either an answering machine for voice mail. I have not received that email conformation. A Whirlpool box arrived on 6 December and I arranged for the technician to make the repairs on December 11. When the technician arrived and opened the box, only one of the two parts had been delivered. There had been no communication from Whirlpool advising me that one of the parts had been backordered and there was no invoice on the box. On December 12th I submitted a customer comment on your website and asked that I be called. On December 13th I called twice and both times was disconnected both times. On December 14th I talked to Danielle. At first she advised that the order had been completed. Then, on further checking she noted that the rear tub shell had been back ordered. She could not give an estimated time when it would arrive. When I asked why no one had contacted me to advise me that one of the parts was back ordered, she stated that that was not Whirlpool policy. When I asked if someone could call me when the part arrived she stated that could not do that. While I understand that an extended warranty is available and would have protected me, I believe that what is supposed to be a top of the line washer should not have major problems within two years of purchase. As there are only two of us at home, it is not that the washer is getting heavy use. But, what is more discouraging to me is what I perceive as an unacceptable level of customer service.

Worst washing machine we ever owned.. Machine is a little over 2 years old and we still cannot get the water temperature correct. You get either cold or warm. So I took him up on the deal, ultimately paying $475 after tax, and so far I'm very happy with its performance. I usually have two or three people who rent rooms in my house. The old washer took 40 gallons of water per load. The Frigidaire takes just 15 gallons! So right off the bat I'm going to be saving a lot on my water bill, as well as a few bucks on electricity as this washer takes less of that to operate, too. The controls are pretty simple to figure out. Ten cycles, four temperature settings, you can set how fast you want the basket to spin, and there's a few extra options, too. Shut the door, hit start, and let it go. Just be sure to remember that you must use HE (High Efficiency) detergent. The wash is very quiet and the spin dry sucks the water right out of the clothes. I can dry my stuff in half the time! I did encounter one problem twice. When washing my bed sheets and blankets, I heard a beeping noise. The washer was stopped and I thought it was done, but it turns out my sheets were still soaked. I looked at the manual and apparently if the load in the washer basket becomes uneven, it won't spin (that's why it was beeping). So I just pushed the blankets a few times, shut the door, and on the cycle dial there's an option for Final Spin, which is just that, the final spin dry. So I selected that, hit start, and it worked both times. I haven't had that problem with any other load of laundry before or after that. This was my first foray into the world of front load washers and so far I'm very pleased with the results! It's quiet, efficient, my clothes are clean and smell fresh, and most important of all to me, it isn't tearing my clothes like my old washer was. And for the price I got it at, it's a great value!

Here is my anecdotal experience with Electrolux front load washers. I spent a day and a half trying to fix my 6-year-old Electrolux model EIFLS60JIW1 which we inherited with our new home 3 months ago. To summarize quickly, I am now in the market for a new washer because I was unable to fix it and may have hastened its demise. So if you are curious, continue reading for details. Also, let me say I think getting 6 years of this unit seems ok but I googled around to try to get a sense of how long these units should last and came up with estimates between 10-14 years, but to be fair I think in my case I probably went about the repair wrong in the end and this is one of those regrettable times where I may have actually caused my unit's demise too which is why I am conflicted about how many stars to give. Also, since they no longer make this version I am listing it with the new models above, not so much to warn other consumers like me but maybe to just inform everyone of my anecdotal experience. Besides, from what I can tell looking around on the internet, the Electrolux brand seems to still be highly rated or at least advertised strategically very well because I am no longer sure what to make of all of those "consumer report" websites which seem more and more biased lately after you google, "best front load washer to buy." Ok so back to focusing on the washer; so it was apparently purchased by the previous owners in July 2015 and appears to have worked fine until now as far as I can tell basically for 6 years. I noticed there was a very small pool of water under and in front of it over the past few days doing 1-2 loads per day. On closer inspection, I saw the door seal had a small part missing portion of rubber where the glass door presses into, spanning about 2 inches in the lower-left portion of the seal so ordered the part from Amazon and replaced it (more on that later). What really prompted us to act was after the small leak got bigger and I noticed at the same time the clothes were still soaked at the end of a cycle. After watching a full 14 min rinse spin cycle finally determined that the thing was not agitating or spinning at all but towards the end of the cycle could hear the motor kick on and sounded like it turning at full speed but still not spinning. Using a very helpful, I have to admit set of videos from repair clinic and appliance parts.com on youtube as a guide, I took back panel off and saw belt had fallen off. After inspecting the belt for cracks I decided to re-install the belt back onto the rotor wheel (mistake perhaps?..should have ordered a new belt, and wheel probably) which was finally feasible after attaching a zip tie to hold a portion of the belt onto the wheel and stretching the rest on. Of note, the wheel itself was also wobbling so found the bolt had loosened and assumed this was responsible for belt eventually falling off in the first place. After tightening the bolt, put back panel on and it worked great again for 4-5 loads then the same problem occured again. As an aside, while working on this portion of the washer, the door boot seal also came in the mail so I also took off the old rubber seal and reinstalled the new seal. To my disappointment, it still seemed to leak even with the new seal. I do not know if this was due to a defective seal or leaking from a different portion of the washer underneath (related to the stuff going on in the back) where I can't see but I did a double-take and re-inspected my installation for what its worth to confirm that the seal and springs holding it on appeared snug. Anyway, for this reason, I am recusing myself from writing a review on the boot seal since I am not sure on the cause of the leak. Fast-forwarding backs up to the back of the washer with the belt falling off. So reading online the most common causes seemed to be worn chewed-up belts, a loose wheel (despite re-tightening), or bearings going within the tub itself. I found the wheel itself was loose again and this time there was a lot more black powder-rubber dust stuff all over the back of the tub. Looked like the belt had been rubbing against the back of the plastic tub and the metal wheel itself had actually cut deeply and completely through the tub like a blade near the top portions of the tub. There was now evidence of water dripping out of where the cuts were and pooling in the tray in the back of the washer! I think in retrospect, I should have probably tried to replace the wheel itself and the belt too because thinking back, the wheel was difficult to wrench back on, and even after tightening there was ever so slight bit of play where the wheel attached to the nut. In conclusion, I like to do my own repairs when there is time to learn more and tinker, and admittedly I sometimes struggle with "repair guy trust issues" (my own demons I am working through), but looking back this was a "penny-wise" move on my part not getting an appliance professional in to do the repair because now the cost of fixing this will approach just replacing the unit. Also, I want to apologize to the Michigan-based repair clinic and appliance parts .com. I used their youtube videos to do the repairs which were excellent. I thought about it and SHOULD have bought the parts from them as well and not gotten cheap and got the less expensive part from Amazon (97$ vs 140 + 27 one day ship). Steam fresh a joke. Before purchasing this washer/dryer combo I owned a Whirlpool duet at my previous home. I thought I would try this LG since it got good reviews and when you view these machines in the store they are very sturdy and well-made. If you are buying this machine for the "steamfresh" feature because like me you don't want to iron shirts that laid in the dryer too long--don't! The cycle takes 20 mins to run, then it "fluffs" the clothes for 30 mins, then after removing them from the washer the manual says to allow the damp clothes to hang for 10 mins before wearing. ??? Now an hour has passed and you could've just ironed them or thrown them in the dryer would've done just as well! Not at all like the commercial! My shirt came out too wet to wear (as it mentioned) and looked as if water had been squirted radomly on it. After all that, I ended up putting it in the dryer. The manual suggested you don't put 100% cotton clothes for the steamfresh either--which is exactly what i bought it for! (My husband's golf shirts) As far as the steamwash feature--if you need your clothes shot full of hot steam because your clothes are unsanitary then you may need this. However, I used the steamwash today on hot water WITH bleach (I might add this cycle took 1 hr and 15 mins) and it still didn't get my socks clean! It works fine to use as a regular washer, but my opinion is it isn't worth the extra $300 I paid full these extra features. Also, the LG is very loud compared to the Whirlpool Duet. It has a loud whining sound when it gets ramped up. The first time I heard it I thought there was a motorcyle going by outside.

They said (in a nasty, condescending tone), "you should have bought the extended warranty, shouldn't you!" I wish I had my old GE washer and dryer units back.
